_README: Verified exam-board facts. Every entry was read from the board's own published document on the date shown, and the URL is recorded so the next person can re-open it rather than trust this file. Nothing goes in here that was settled from memory. If a fact cannot be sourced, it belongs in _unverified, not here.

aqa-gcse-business-8132.name: AQA GCSE Business 8132

section_names.3.6.3: Financial terms and calculations (includes average rate of return and break-even)
section_names.3.6.4: Analysing the financial performance of a business (includes gross and net profit margin)
section_names.3.1.1: The purpose and nature of businesses

aqa-gcse-business-8132.papers: Paper 1 and Paper 2, each 1 hour 45 minutes, 90 marks, 50%

excluded_content.quote: Students will not be expected to draw break-even charts or use the break-even formula.
the word 'contribution' does not appear anywhere in the specification
Specific motivational theories (such as Maslow) will not be examined.

aqa-alevel-business-7132.name: AQA A-level Business 7132
notes: Section 3.1 ends at 3.1.3. Codes 3.1.4, 3.1.5 and 3.1.6 do not exist.
3.1 to 3.6 is the AS content. AQA labels 3.7 to 3.10 '(A-level only)'.
Markets and market research are 3.3.2; positioning is 3.3.3; added value is an operational objective at 3.4.1.
aqa-alevel-business-7132.command_words_note: Assess and Recommend are not on AQA's published list. Evaluate IS on the list even though recent papers have used Justify and To what extent for evaluative questions.

9-mark.note: no AO4, so no judgement required

section_names.3.6.4: Making human resource decisions: improving motivation and engagement
section_names.3.7.4: Analysing the external environment: political and legal change
section_names.3.7.6: Analysing the external environment: social and technological change

aqa-alevel-business-7138.name: AQA A-level Business 7138
aqa-alevel-business-7138.status: first teaching September 2026. AS first assessment May/June 2027, A-level first assessment May/June 2028
aqa-alevel-business-7138.papers: three papers, each 2 hours, 90 marks, 33.3%. Total scaled mark 270.
notes: Top tariff on any question is 15. There is no 25-mark essay and no 16-mark question.
'To what extent' and 'Justify' are not command words in 7138.
Evaluate is a two-option question ending in a recommendation.
aqa-alevel-business-7138.status_quote: Assessments and certification for the A-level specification are available for the first time in May/June 2028 and then every May/June for the life of the specification.

units.3.1: What is business? Managing marketing and finance
units.3.3: Business and society, business and the external environment and business strategy

papers_alevel.Paper 1: Unit 3.1. Written exam 2 hours, 90 marks, 33.3%. Two case studies, each followed by five compulsory questions worth 45 marks in total.
papers_alevel.Paper 2: Unit 3.2 with links to Unit 3.1. Written exam 2 hours, 90 marks, 33.3%. Two case studies, each followed by five compulsory questions worth 45 marks in total.
papers_alevel.Paper 3: Unit 3.3 with links to Units 3.1 and 3.2. Written exam 2 hours, 90 marks, 33.3%. Two case studies, each followed by five compulsory questions worth 45 marks in total.

papers_as.Paper 1: AS content in Unit 3.1. Written exam 1 hour 45 minutes, 80 marks, 50% of AS. Two case studies, each followed by six compulsory questions worth 40 marks in total.
papers_as.Paper 2: AS content in Unit 3.2 with links to Unit 3.1. Written exam 1 hour 45 minutes, 80 marks, 50% of AS. Two case studies, each followed by six compulsory questions worth 40 marks in total.

ao_weightings_alevel.per_paper: AO1 8.14, AO2 8.14, AO3 8.89, AO4 8.14 on each of the three papers

command_word_definitions.Define: Knowledge and understanding only. (AO1). 2 marks, AS assessment only.
command_word_definitions.Explain: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of a business term/concept in the context of the case study material provided. (AO1 and AO2). 4 marks, AS assessment only.
command_word_definitions.Analyse: Analyse an issue in the context of the case study material provided. (AO1, AO2, AO3). 6 marks.
command_word_definitions.Assess: Assess the arguments for and against a particular issue and make a judgement. For example, learners may be asked whether a single particular action is right for a business. Learners will be weighing up the arguments for and against the action or issue presented and then deciding which argument is stronger. This question type requires a judgement. (AO1, AO2, AO3, AO4). 9 marks.
command_word_definitions.Evaluate: There are two types of evaluate questions: A) Learners are required to identify and evaluate two possible courses of action to solve a particular problem or opportunity facing a business and make a recommendation as to which is most suitable B) Learners are required to evaluate two options presented in the question and make a judgement of which the business should choose. (AO1, AO2, AO3, AO4). 15 marks.

aqa-alevel-business-7138.extended_response_quote: 15-mark questions in both AS and A-level papers assess learners' ability to analyse, evaluate, and make judgements. In A-level Paper 3, extended responses take a strategic view, asking learners to solve a business problem or recommend a course of action to achieve a specific outcome.
aqa-alevel-business-7138.synoptic_quote: Synopticity occurs when learners draw on knowledge from different parts of the specification. This is especially relevant in AS paper 2 and A-level paper 3.
aqa-alevel-business-7138.scaling: Each A-level paper 90 raw marks, scaling factor x1, total scaled mark 270.

edexcel-alevel-business-9bs0.name: Pearson Edexcel A-level Business 9BS0
edexcel-alevel-business-9bs0.status_quote: learners beginning the course in September 2026 will continue to follow the current established specification
edexcel-alevel-business-9bs0.command_words_note: Analyse, Justify, Discuss and To what extent do not appear in the 9BS0 sample assessment materials.

20-mark.stem: Evaluate these two options and recommend which one is most suitable for [business] to [objective]
20-mark.ao_split_note: Pearson publishes AO weightings only as ranges at qualification and paper level. There is NO published per-question AO split for the 20-mark question. Any 4/4/6/6 split is an inference and must be labelled as the author's own.

section_names.1.5.4: Forms of business (includes growth to plc and stock market flotation)

edexcel-gcse-business-1bs0.name: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Business 1BS0
edexcel-gcse-business-1bs0.papers: two papers, each 1 hour 45 minutes, 90 marks, 50%. Sections A 35, B 30, C 25.

command_word_definitions.Justify: write an extended answer, using information provided in order to recommend one of two options to a business owner
command_word_definitions.Analyse: write an extended answer, requiring expansion and exploration of a business concept or issue. The answer will be placed in context by the question

9-mark.note: Pearson prints '(9) AO2=3 AO3a=3 AO3b=3'. Every level, Level 1 included, requires a judgement.

ocr-alevel-business-h431.name: OCR A Level Business H431
ocr-alevel-business-h431.command_words_note: OCR publishes no command word list in its specification. The tariffs below are read off all three June 2024 mark schemes and are one series, not a rule.
ocr-alevel-business-h431.note: OCR's biggest questions are on Paper 3, the global business environment: a 20-mark Evaluate and a 20-mark Discuss, both over four levels at 1-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16-20. Reading only Papers 1 and 2 gives the wrong answer.

cambridge-igcse-economics-0455.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455

2027-2029.marking: levels of response on the 8-mark part (d) only; everything else point marked, including the 6-mark Analyse

cambridge-igcse-economics-0455.note: A class starting September 2026 sits exams in 2028, so it is on the 2027 to 2029 syllabus. Any resource written to the 2026 syllabus must say so.

cambridge-igcse-business-0450.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
cambridge-igcse-business-0450.replacement_quote: We have changed the syllabus code to 0264 for first assessment March 2027
cambridge-igcse-business-0450.command_words_note: Evaluate, Assess, Discuss and Analyse are NOT 0450 command words.

excluded_content.quote: profit is not a method of measuring business size
knowledge of the formula and calculations of PED will not be assessed
constructing income statements will not be assessed
constructing statements of financial position will not be assessed
exchange rate calculations will not be assessed

btec-l3-national-business.name: Pearson BTEC Level 3 National in Business

command_verb_definitions.Justify: Learners give reasons or evidence to: support an opinion; or prove something right or reasonable.
command_verb_definitions.Analyse: breaking down a theme, topic or situation in order to interpret and study the interrelationships between the parts
command_verb_definitions.Assess: a careful consideration of varied factors or events that apply to a specific situation or, to identify those which are the most important or relevant and arrive at a conclusion
command_verb_definitions.Evaluate: leads to a supported judgement showing relationship to its context

btec-l3-national-business.justify_note: Justify does NOT mean choosing the best of several options. Both Justify criteria in the specification justify a single thing: D1 justifies the research methods a business used, D4 justifies its use of innovation.
btec-l3-national-business.verb_by_band_note: The ladder holds as a rule, not an absolute. Assess appears at Distinction as well as Merit.

aims.A: Explore the features of different businesses and analyse what makes them successful
aims.E: Investigate the role and contribution of innovation and enterprise to business success

btec-tech-award-enterprise-2022.name: Pearson BTEC Level 1/Level 2 Tech Award in Enterprise (2022)

2.title: Planning and Presenting a Micro-Enterprise Idea

3.title: Marketing and Finance for Enterprise
3.type: External synoptic exam, externally marked, 2 hours

internal_assessment_model.uses: Mark Bands 0 to 4 against Learning outcomes
internal_assessment_model.does_not_use: Pass / Merit / Distinction criteria, criteria codes such as A.2P1 or B.2M2, or 'learning aims'
internal_assessment_model.evidence: In Pearson's own 2022 Component 2 Pearson-set Assignment the words Pass, Merit, Distinction, criteria, 2P1, 2M1 and 2D1 appear ZERO times, while 'Mark Band' appears 48 times and 'Learning outcome' 7 times.
internal_assessment_model.warning: The Pass/Merit/Distinction criteria-and-command-verb model belongs to the PREVIOUS (2017) Tech Award. Do not describe the 2022 award that way.

btec-tech-award-enterprise-2022.spec_note: Issue 7, May 2026, 82 pages. The URL Pearson search returns, with the 603/7063/4 prefix, 404s; this one works. In this document Mark Band appears 70 times, learning outcome 4 times, and learning aim and "Pass, Merit" ZERO times.

grade_scale.qualification: seven grades, Level 2 Distinction* down to Level 1 Pass
grade_scale.component: six grades, Level 2 Distinction down to Level 1 Pass, no star
grade_scale.quote: The BTEC Tech Award qualifications will be graded and certificated on a seven-grade scale from Level 2 Distinction* to Level 1 Pass. Individual components will be graded on a six-point scale from Level 2 Distinction to Level 1 Pass.

ib-business-management.name: IB Diploma Programme Business Management
ib-business-management.toolkit: Business management toolkit, a SEPARATE component with 35 recommended hours. It is not Unit 6 and carries no code such as 6.1.
ib-business-management.warning: ibo.org's public curriculum page still shows the PREVIOUS syllabus outline, where 1.5 is External environment. Cite the subject brief, not the web page.

aqa-alevel-economics-7136.name: AQA A-level Economics 7136

papers.Paper 1: Markets and market failure. Content 1 to 8. Written exam 2 hours, 80 marks, 33.3%. Section A data response requiring written answers, choice of one from two contexts worth 40 marks. Section B essay questions requiring written answers, choice of one from three worth 40 marks.
papers.Paper 2: National and international economy. Content 9 to 14. Written exam 2 hours, 80 marks, 33.3%. Same section structure as Paper 1.
papers.Paper 3: Economic principles and issues. All content 1 to 14. Written exam 2 hours, 80 marks, 33.3%. Section A multiple choice questions worth 30 marks. Section B case study questions requiring written answers, worth 50 marks.

aqa-alevel-economics-7136.papers_note: All the question papers are compulsory. Total scaled mark 240.

ao_weightings_alevel.per_paper: Paper 1 and Paper 2: AO1 5-8, AO2 7-10, AO3 9-11, AO4 7-10. Paper 3: AO1 7-10, AO2 9-12, AO3 6-9, AO4 5-8.

aqa-alevel-economics-7136.quantitative_minimum: at least Level 2 mathematical skills as a minimum of 20% of the overall A-level marks, and 15% at AS
quantitative_skills: calculate, use and understand ratios and fractions
calculate, use and understand percentages and percentage changes
understand and use the terms mean, median and relevant quantiles
construct and interpret a range of standard graphical forms
calculate cost, revenue and profit (marginal, average, totals)
make calculations to convert from money to real terms
make calculations of elasticity and interpret the result
interpret, apply and analyse information in written, graphical and numerical forms

paper1_june_2023.section_a: Each context: 2 marks calculate, 4 marks Explain, 9 marks Explain with the help of a diagram, 25 marks Evaluate. Total for this context 40 marks.
paper1_june_2023.section_b: Each essay: a 15-mark Explain, then a 25-mark question. Total for this essay 40 marks.

grid_25.heading_quote: Below is the levels of response marking grid to be used when marking any 25-mark question.
grid_25.top_band_quote: Sound, focused analysis and well-supported evaluation that: is well organised, showing sound knowledge and understanding of economic terminology, concepts and principles with few, if any, errors; includes good application of relevant economic principles to the given context and, where appropriate, good use of data to support the response; includes well-focused analysis with clear, logical chains of reasoning; includes supported evaluation throughout the response and in a final conclusion.

grid_15.heading_quote: Below is the levels of response marking grid which should be used to mark the 15-mark questions
grid_15.top_band_quote: A good response provides an answer that: is well organised and develops a selection of the key issues that are relevant to the question; shows sound knowledge and understanding of economic terminology, concepts and principles with few, if any, errors; includes good application of relevant economic principles to the given context and, where appropriate, good use of data to support the response; includes well-focused analysis with clear, logical chains of reasoning.
grid_15.evaluation: The word evaluation does not appear anywhere in the 15-mark grid. All three levels stop at analysis.

edexcel-alevel-economics-9ec0.name: Pearson Edexcel A level Economics A, 9EC0
edexcel-alevel-economics-9ec0.source_type: Pearson Getting Started guide for the 2015 specification

themes.1: Introduction to markets and market failure
themes.2: The UK economy, performance and policies
themes.3: Business behaviour and the labour market

papers.Paper 1: Markets and business behaviour. Questions drawn from Theme 1 and Theme 3. 100 marks, 35%, 2 hours. Section A multiple-choice and short-answer, all questions. Section B based on stimulus material, one data response question comprising a number of parts. Section C one extended open-response question, one from a choice of two.
papers.Paper 2: The national and global economy. Questions drawn from Theme 2 and Theme 4. 100 marks, 35%, 2 hours. Same section structure as Paper 1.
papers.Paper 3: Microeconomics and macroeconomics. Questions drawn from all themes. 100 marks, 30%, 2 hours. Sections A and B are each based on stimulus material, each one data response question comprising a number of parts, each including one extended open-response question chosen from two.

edexcel-alevel-economics-9ec0.papers_quote: There are three A level papers, each comprising 100 marks and 2 hours in duration.
edexcel-alevel-economics-9ec0.quantitative_minimum: a minimum of 20% of the total marks across the A level and 15% of total marks across the AS level

extended_response_commands.Assess: Accurate knowledge and understanding; apply to context and/or use relevant examples; use of economic theory applied appropriately; and evaluation which is supported by chains of reasoning, in context and balanced.
extended_response_commands.Discuss: Accurate knowledge and understanding; apply to context and/or use relevant examples; use of economic theory applied appropriately; logical chains of reasoning; and evaluation which is supported by relevant reasoning, in context and balanced.
extended_response_commands.To what extent / Evaluate: Accurate knowledge and understanding; apply to context and/or use relevant examples; evidence fully and reliably integrated; use of economic theory applied appropriately; logical and coherent chains of reasoning; and evaluation which is supported by chains of reasoning, in context, with critical awareness and informed judgements.

edexcel-alevel-economics-9ec0.commands_note: Pearson groups 'To what extent' and 'Evaluate' as a single row in the Getting Started taxonomy table. Assess and Discuss are listed separately. The guide gives no mark tariffs against these commands.
edexcel-alevel-economics-9ec0.section_ao_note: Section A assesses breadth, with a greater focus on AO1 and AO2. Section B is based on stimulus material and places greater emphasis on depth (AO3 and AO4).
